commit.message:
test(cli): cancel at observed points, not after a fixed 500 ms (#146)

SubmitCancelTimeoutP05Tests fired the user cancel 500 ms after start. Under load the timer can fire before the submit loop holds the build ID, so the CLI correctly takes the before-ID path (no cancel RPC) and the after-ID cases fail with CancelledBuildIds empty (v0.9.1 release prep, Rocky8 full suite). The same race made the WhileSubmitInFlight case fail when Submit had not reached the server yet.

The user cancel now fires at an observed point: the fake server holding Resolve or Submit for the before-ID cases, and the output loop printing the first watch event for the after-ID cases. The loop is sequential and receives the build ID before any watch event, so that line proves the build ID is held. A 30 s bound only ends a run whose point is never reached, and the test then fails on the barrier assertion. No production change.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix(cli): cancel function-recipe create on /cancel (P10.executable, S4-04-C) (#141)

* fix(cli): cancel function-recipe create on /cancel (P10.executable, S4-04-C)

S4-04-C asks that explicit cancel during redirected interactive
authoring exits 130, saves no file and writes no ANSI to machine
streams. recipe create already handled /cancel, /quit and /exit, but
function-recipe create stored them as field values.

Every function-recipe create prompt now treats /cancel, /quit and /exit
(RecipeCreateEscapeCommands.IsCancel) as cancel. The command prints the
same notice and returns 130 before any write, so no Recipe and no
.nodekit-lock are left. The wizard shows a /cancel hint. EOF handling
is unchanged.

Tests: in-process cancel at required and optional prompts, and
published-process cancel for both recipe create and function-recipe
create (exit 130, empty work dir, no ANSI).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): honour /cancel at the function-recipe create save-path prompt (P10.executable, S4-04-C)

Codex review r4323346149 on PR141: without an output path, function-recipe create asks for the save path after the wizard returns. That prompt read a raw line outside the RecipeCreateCancelledException handler, so /cancel was taken as the path "/cancel" and the command failed with a write error instead of exiting 130.

PromptForPath now calls RecipeCreateEscapeCommands.ThrowIfCancel, and the prompt runs inside the existing cancel handler. /cancel, /quit and /exit (trimmed) at the save-path prompt print the usual notice and return 130 with no Recipe and no .nodekit-lock. EOF and blank input still mean the default path, and a path that merely contains "cancel" is still saved.

Tests: in-process save-path cancel for /cancel, /quit, /exit and a padded /cancel; an entered path still saves; published-process save-path /cancel (exit 130, save prompt shown, empty CWD, no ANSI) and save-path EOF (saves the default file in the CWD).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

EOF at a required prompt (functionId, revision, script path, executable,

script 1, A's absolute script path 2 without rewrite, unsupported SchemaVersion
2, all RPC 0 and no CWD fallback. Editing the Recipe on B and resubmitting binds
a new source snapshot and leaves the earlier receipt and snapshots unchanged.

the transcript now records install_dir and record_dir.

AssertNoReferenceTo read every B file as plain text, so A's absolute DockerfilePath stored base64-encoded in .nodekit/snapshots/source (content_base64) was invisible to it (Codex r4315112685, Guardrail B-P1). The DockerfilePath allowance is scoped by Recipe logical path: exactly once in dockerfile.json and once in the snapshot entry with logical_path dockerfile.json, nowhere else. A package-free self-test pins the checker: it must catch an A path or endpoint inside an encoded entry, an allowance under a different logical path, a second A path next to the allowed value, and a plain-file endpoint. * fix(cli): let the WhenAny winner decide the registration outcome (P08.timeout)

Codex P2 r4302438283: Call() discarded the Task.WhenAny result and then
re-read rpc.IsCompleted. If the timeout or Ctrl-C won but the response
finished before that read, a late success was classified and stored as
registered, against registration_late_ack.

Settle() now accepts the RPC result only when the RPC task won. The
decision point is internal so the race window, which cannot be
reproduced in-process, is tested directly: abort won + response already

* feat(cli): typed RegisterToolFunction after the second image build (P08.registry)

v0.9.1 S3-07-A..G. After `function-recipe submit` verifies a full second
image digest B, the CLI now sends the typed registration:

- P06 mapper -> RegisterToolFunctionRequest (w2-set-v1, C1, B, typed
  groups). Its exact protobuf bytes and a prepared receipt are written
  under the same record root (registrations/<id>.json,
  snapshots/registration/<sha256>.bin) before any RPC; a store failure

  missing/corrupt F or H -> unknown (exit 1), never resubmitted under a
  new id or version. A receipt write failure after a normal response is
  exit 2 with the observed values only in the diagnostic.
- `function-recipe register-replay <receipt>` resends only the stored
  endpoint/id/version/bytes; it never re-reads the Recipe or script and
  never builds. registered/rejected replays show the stored result.
- jsonl: with registration, build success is a `state` record and the
  single `completed` comes from registration (additive fields).

BuildService/ToolRegistryService. Build-only injection (P07 tests)
still stops after the build. Registration timeout/Ctrl-C is P08.timeout.

feat(cli): raw_spec v1 serializer + typed ToolFunctionSpec registration mapper (P06.raw_typed) (#125)

* feat(cli): raw_spec v1 serializer + typed ToolFunctionSpec registration mapper (P06.raw_typed)

- ToolFunctionRawSpecFactory: exact 4-key nodevault.build.raw_spec.v1
  payload (schema_version, kind=2, base_image_digest=A, script content)
  plus a boundary validator that rejects kind strings, schema typos,
  extra/duplicate keys, blank scripts and trailing content (S3-04-A/B/D/E).
- ToolFunctionRegistrationRequestFactory: Recipe -> RegisterToolFunctionRequest
  with explicit name-based enum maps (no numeric cast, unknown values
  rejected), C1 bare-64-lower-hex guard, B required, C2 kept outside the
  request, canonicalization_version w2-set-v1, unset optionals left
  unspecified, output-note orphan/duplicate rejection (S3-02-A/D/E/F, S3-06).
- ToolFunctionBaseLinkEvidence: OBSERVED_SAME_BUILD only for a complete
  same-build observation that matches C1/A exactly; otherwise
  MANUAL_UNVERIFIED. Never a server-authoritative link claim.

No RPC, caller wiring or render/submit gate here (P06.current/P07/P08).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): reject ports whose direction conflicts with their list (Codex P2)

A port with Direction=Output inside InputPorts (or the reverse) was mapped
by its containing list with the wrong direction-specific fields. Reject it
with PORT_DIRECTION_MISMATCH (exit 1) before building the request.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): map an empty timeout group like no timeout (P06.raw_typed P2-1)

An L1-valid Recipe with an empty timeoutPolicy object, or one whose soft and
hard values are 0, mapped to a present-but-empty timeout_policy. NodeVault's
canonicalizer keeps that apart from an absent one, so two Recipes that both
mean "no timeout" got different ToolFunction digests. Emit timeout_policy only
when soft or hard is non-zero (0 = unset, N1), and pin the empty-group variants
through save/reload/L1/map (S3-06-C). Also add the trailing-LF variant to the
malformed B list (S3-02-D).

feat(cli): durable local operation journal and receipt (P04.store, S2-02) (#118)

* feat(cli): durable local operation journal and receipt (P04.store, S2-02)

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* test(cli): use string theory data for P04 store fault cases

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): P04.store endpoint gate, receipt-root discovery and snapshot integrity checks

Bounded correction for PR118 review (Guardrail P2x2, Codex r4236850904/
r4236850910/r4236850912):
- RunAsync takes the actual endpoint and refuses a stored request whose
  endpoint differs with OPERATION_RECORD_MISMATCH/2 before Resolve (RPC0).
- RootForReceipt/ForReceipt derive the snapshot root from a receipt path;
  create/open refuse a receipt whose root is not this store.
- Snapshot IDs must be lowercase SHA-256 hex before use as a path; a
  malformed ID is OPERATION_RECORD_INVALID instead of an exception.
- The resolved snapshot must be bound to the receipt's source/envelope/
  requested tool and version.
- Advance validates the next receipt before writing it.
- Regressions for the endpoint gate, Advance guards (phase, build_id,
  resolved snapshot), ack/terminal build_id requirement, missing and
  tampered snapshots, foreign resolved snapshot and malformed IDs.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): bind resolved snapshots to their attempt and require a terminal observation

Codex r4237094648: ResolvedSnapshot now stores request_id and endpoint, and
TryOpen rejects a receipt whose resolved snapshot belongs to another attempt
or endpoint (OPERATION_RECORD_INVALID/2, no RPC).

Codex r4237094654: a terminal receipt without last_observation is invalid on
open and is never written by Advance.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): exact receipt field sets per phase, reject other builds' watch events, keep terminal kind

- ValidateReceipt checks the exact field set of every phase: a prepared
  record with a build_id, an observation or a resolved-snapshot pointer
  (or an in-flight/acknowledged record with later-phase fields) is
  OPERATION_RECORD_INVALID/2 instead of being re-run as fresh.
- The runner stops with exit 1, without persisting, when a watch event
  names a build other than the acknowledged one.
- A terminal event without status records Succeeded/Failed from its kind
  instead of keeping the previous status.
- Test fixture: submit and watch now report the same build.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* P04.store: validate source snapshot entries and keep SpecReferrerDigest

Codex r4237295515: every SourceSnapshot entry must decode from base64 and match its declared lowercase SHA-256. TryCreateToolSpecOperation refuses a malformed source before any file is written, and TryReadSourceSnapshot (also used on reopen) rejects it as OPERATION_RECORD_INVALID/exit 2 with no RPC.

Codex r4237295517: OperationObservation now stores spec_referrer_digest, copied from WatchToolBuild events and carried forward, so a reopened terminal receipt still names the ToolSpec referrer artifact.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): reject blank envelope fields and terminal records without an outcome

Codex P2 r4237570256: ToolName/Version/RawSpec must be nonblank when an
operation is created and when its receipt is reopened. The envelope hash
only matches itself, so a blank field passed validation and Resolve was
sent with an empty request field. Both paths now return
OPERATION_RECORD_INVALID (exit 2) before any write or RPC.

Codex P2 r4237570258: a terminal receipt now carries last_observation.outcome
(Succeeded/Failed) taken from the terminal watch event kind, and
ValidateReceipt rejects terminal records whose outcome is missing, empty or
any other value such as Running. The server status (e.g. Interrupted) is
kept as reported.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Co-authored-by: HeaInSeo <seoyhaein@gmail.com>

commit.message:
feat(cli): add P02 atomic file writer foundation (#112)

* feat(cli): P02.writer_foundation atomic file writer

Add AtomicFileWriter, the shared save boundary for the later
create/validate/render callers (cli-acceptance-contract supportProfile).
Callers are not switched in this stage (P02.writer_caller).

- same-directory temp file, full write, Flush(flushToDisk), then rename
- cross-process writer exclusion via a persistent .<name>.nodekit-lock
  (FileShare.None = flock on Unix); contention -> WRITE_LOCKED exit 2
- any IO/permission fault before rename keeps the old bytes; exit 2
- cancellation before the commit point -> exit 130, old bytes kept
- directory/symlink target or missing parent -> exit 2 before overwrite,
  no copy/delete fallback
- stale temp files left by a killed writer are removed under the lock,
  matching only the exact temp shape of the same target
- existing Unix file mode is kept

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* fix(cli): reject FIFO/socket/device targets before atomic replace

Codex P2 on #112: an existing FIFO, socket or device passed the
target check (FileInfo.Exists=true, LinkTarget=null), so the rename
replaced it with a regular file and reported success. Check the file
type with statx(2) on Linux and return WRITE_TARGET_UNSUPPORTED (exit 2)
before any temp file or rename. statx has a fixed, architecture-independent
layout; outside the supported Linux profile the check is skipped.

Also give TryDelete non-empty catch bodies (CodeQL empty catch block).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
